target_resolution_m_at_46_5N.note: 512-px tile m/pix at latitude 46.5 N = 53892 / 2^z. z12 (13.2 m/pix) is safely coarser than the 10 m TINITALY source; z13 (6.6 m/pix) would upsample beyond the 0.7x-source honesty guideline.

void_fill.method: TINITALY where valid, else Copernicus GLO-30 reprojected with bilinear resampling to the same tile grid; cosine cross-fade on ground distance to the TINITALY nodata edge (distance transform), weights only, no synthetic heights
void_fill.low_zoom_note: at z6-z8 a tile pixel (105-840 m) is wider than the feather, so the seam is effectively a hard switch there

datum_handling.glo30: EGM2008 (EPSG:3855), Copernicus DEM Product Handbook v5.0 sec. 1.2
datum_handling.tinitaly: not stated by the provider; interpolated from topographic contours and spot heights
datum_handling.empirical_check: TINITALY minus GLO-30 over 8 793 913 valid TINITALY cells (50 m sampling) in the bbox: median -3.25 m, p25 -11.15 m, p75 +0.69 m; within 0-300 m of the TINITALY edge median +0.9 to +1.7 m. An ellipsoidal source would show ~47 m.

caveats: North of the Italian border (and in the other TINITALY voids) heights are GLO-30: a ~30 m surface model including forest canopy and buildings. At z12 (and partly z11) these tiles are bilinear interpolations of 30 m data, smooth and without 13 m detail; do not present them as 13 m data.

verification.method: (a) read back tiles at z=8, 10, 12 at the bbox centre, decode Terrain-RGB, compare the centre pixel with the raw TINITALY cell at that point; (b) at z=12, decode the pixel containing three Austrian points (compared with GLO-30, nearest source cell) and three Italian points (compared with TINITALY, nearest source cell)
verification.expected_error: |diff| of a few metres = 0.1 m Terrain-RGB quantisation + bilinear resampling of a 10 m (TINITALY) or 30 m (GLO-30) grid onto 13-53 m Web Mercator pixels, compared against a single nearest source cell; larger on steep slopes
